speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you've brought in your infant with bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and an inability to pass meconium. To confirm the suspicion of intestinal obstruction, can you tell me exactly how old your baby is in days or weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease. Given the classic triad of bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and failure to pass meconium in a 2-day-old infant born via home birth, I request an urgent Rectal_Swab for acetylcholinesterase staining and an Abdominal_X-Ray to confirm the diagnosis.
